messages:
Maria H: Quick heads-up — after the OTel SDK bump on the background-worker image (python svc) I'm seeing a bunch of child ops with no parent in Jaeger for the async queue jobs. Not all requests, maybe ~20%.
Devon K: Which SDK version did we move to? any change in propagators or sampler?
Maria H: We moved from opentelemetry-python 1.10 -> 1.13. No intentional config changes but the image also switched HTTP client to httpx 0.27.
Samir: Could be default propagators or a race where header gets dropped by the task dispatcher. Can you paste an example trace id/span id pattern?
Maria H: Example traces show root span present on the incoming API call, but worker spans have parent_span_id = 00000000... (null). Dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/dashboard/db/traces?var-service=worker-async
Elin P: Do you still see the traceparent header on the job payload when it lands? maybe our queue serializer drops headers.
Maria H: I grabbed a payload dump:
```
headers: {
  "content-type": "application/json",
  "traceparent": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01"
}
body: {"task": "process_item", "id": 123}
```
But the worker logs show:
```
Received task id=123 traceparent=null
```
Raj S: That screams deserialization or our celery adapter. Which queue lib/version?
Maria H: We're using our in-house queue wrapper on top of redis+rq, wrapper hasn't changed. Only the worker image changed.
Devon K: Double-check OTEL_PROPAGATORS and auto-instrumentation env. In 1.13 defaults might have differed. What's in the worker env now?
Maria H: env shows: `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage` and `OTEL_PYTHON_TRACER_PROVIDER=automatic` set by buildpack.
Samir: If header shows up at enqueue but null in worker, maybe the worker process reads requests from Redis without the header field — confirm the wrapper preserves `headers` map and doesn't stringify then re-parse unexpectedly.
Elin P: Also check httpx version: known issue with async context propagation and background tasks where contextvar propagates poorly across event loop changes. If the enqueuer attaches contextvar metadata instead of raw headers, those won't cross process boundary.
Maria H: Good point. The enqueuer is instrumented and relied on contextvars to add trace info instead of explicitly copying headers. I'll add explicit header propagation in the serializer as a patch.
Devon K: Short checklist to debug quickly:
- verify traceparent present at enqueue (you did)
- verify payload entry in redis contains header key (inspect raw redis entry)
- add temporary logging in worker on message raw payload before any deserialization
- run a manual curl -> enqueue -> worker flow and capture both sides
- if missing, fallback to putting traceparent field in body explicitly
Samir: Also run a local reproduce: start worker and enqueue a job with `traceparent` set, then call `rq info` to fetch raw job data.
Maria H: I'll run the reproduce and post logs here. If we need a short fix, I'll push a serializer change that copies `traceparent` into body.metadata.traceparent and deploy a canary to one worker pool.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: canary/worker-async image v2.3.4 -> rollout started
Raj S: If you push the change, @oncall can we get a fast rollback plan? add a feature flag and keep old behavior if header absent.
Maria H: Will do. Planning to open PR in ~30m. I'll add the test and the redis-inspect debug command.
Elin P: If it looks like httpx/contextvars root cause, we should pin httpx back or upgrade to newer event-loop friendly version. Keep us posted.
Maria H: Thanks — posting logs once I reproduce. :thumbsup:
